1.w: Or are you⁺ ignorant, brothers (for I speak to those knowing the law), that the law rules over the man for as long as the time he lives?

2.w: For the married woman is bound by law to the living husband; but if the husband should die, she is released from the law of the husband.

3.w: So then, of the husband being alive, if she becomes unto another man, she will be called an adulteress; but if the husband should die, she is free from the law, [so as] not for her to be an adulteress, having become unto another man.

4.w: Likewise, my brothers, you⁺ also have been put to death to the law through the body of Christ, for you⁺ to become unto another, unto the One having been raised out from the dead, so that we should bear fruit to God.

5.w: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins that [were] through the law were working in our members, to the bearing of fruit to death.

6.w: But now we have been released from the law, having died to that by which we were held, so as for us to serve in the newness of the Spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

7.w: What then will we say? [Is] the law sin? Never may it be! But I did not know sin, if not through the law. For I would not have been conscious of covetousness if the law had not said, “You shall not covet.”

8.w: But sin, having taken the opportunity through the commandment, produced in me all covetousness; for apart from the law, sin [is] dead.

9.w: And I was once alive apart from the law, but [on] the commandment's having come, sin revived and I died;

10.w: and the commandment that [was] unto life, this was found by me unto death.

11.w: For sin, having taken the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed [me].

12.w: So indeed, the law [is] holy, and the commandment [is] holy and righteous and good.

13.w: Did that which [is] good, then, become death to me? Never may it be! But so that sin might be shown as sin, it is producing death through that which [is] good to me, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond excess.

14.w: For we have known that the law is spiritual; but I am fleshly, having been sold as a slave under sin.

15.w: For what I carry out, I do not understand. For what I want, this I do not practice; but what I hate, this I do.

16.w: Now if what I do not want, this I do, I assent to the law, that [it is] good.

17.w: But now I no longer carry it out, but the sin dwelling in me.

18.w: For I know that there does not dwell in me—that is, in my flesh—good. For to want is present with me, but not to carry out the good.

19.w: For the good that I want, I do not do; but the evil that I do not want, this I practice.

20.w: Now if what I do not want, this I do, no longer do I carry it out, but sin dwelling in me.

21.w: I find, then, the law in my wanting to do good, that evil is present with me.

22.w: For I delight in the law of God according to the inner man,

23.w: but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin being in my members.

24.w: O wretched man [that] I am! Who will deliver me out of this body of death?

25.w: But thanks [be] to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself indeed with the mind serve God’s law, but [with] the flesh the law of sin.
